$comment: Feel layer tuning. Nothing in src/fx/ contains a literal; every magnitude, duration and count is here. M2 combat adds entries to `impacts` rather than adding numbers to code.
$comment_shake: Trauma-based screen shake, the Squirrel Eiserloh model. Callers add trauma 0..1; the offset scales with trauma SQUARED, which is what keeps a light tap subtle while a heavy hit still slams. Linear trauma makes every magnitude feel like the same shake at different volumes.

shake.$comment_decay: Trauma units shed per second. 1.6 means a full-trauma hit is visually done in about 0.6s, which is roughly one harvest swing apart.
shake.$comment_frequency: Noise samples per second. Below about 15 the shake reads as a wobble rather than an impact; above about 30 it reads as a dropped frame.
shake.$comment_maxOffset: Metres of camera displacement at trauma 1. The camera boom is 5.2m, so 0.34 is about 6.5% of the framing: enough to feel, small enough not to lose the target.

$comment_hitPause: Freeze frames. Withholds simulation steps while rendering continues; see src/fx/hitPause.ts for why this may not be done by scaling delta.

hitPause.$comment_maxMs: Hard ceiling on a single freeze. A pause longer than this stops reading as impact and starts reading as a hang, and it is also the guard that keeps repeated hits from compounding into a lockup.

$comment_numbers: Floating numbers are pooled DOM nodes, not meshes, so they cost zero draw calls and inherit tokens.css. The pool is fixed: at capacity the oldest is recycled rather than a new node being created mid-frame.

numbers.$comment_spread: Horizontal metres of deterministic jitter, so two numbers spawned at one point do not stack into an unreadable smear.
numbers.$comment_stagger: A felled rock drops stone AND flint on the same frame at the same point, so horizontal jitter alone is not enough: the two lines overlap and neither is readable. Each number spawned while another is still young is lifted by `staggerMetres`, which reads as a short stack.
numbers.$comment_hideBehindCamera: Numbers spawned behind the camera project to a mirrored on-screen position. Without this check a chop behind you paints a number in front of you.

$comment_particles: One pooled emitter per preset. Systems are built at boot and restarted on emit, because constructing a ParticleSystem mid-frame allocates buffers and shows up as a hitch exactly when something interesting is happening.

particles.$comment_presets: `presets` is iterated by Particles.ts as a pure map of id to preset, so NOTHING but presets may go inside it. Comment keys live at this level. Two notes that would otherwise sit next to their entries: hit_spark is unused until M2, defined now so combat is a call site rather than a new preset plus a tuning pass; and leaf_burst pops up then FALLS, after a first tuning with speed 2.2 against gravity -2.1 left leaves drifting upward for their whole lifetime and reading as rising embers rather than as a tree coming down.

$comment_impacts: The vocabulary of feel. A caller names an impact; it never names a shake magnitude and a particle preset separately, so 'what a felled oak feels like' is one row here rather than four arguments at a call site. M2 adds quick_hit, power_hit, catch_shake, catch_success and orb_break to this table.
$comment_harvest: Which impact each harvestable prop family feels like. Keyed by family rather than by tool action so a future stone tree and a wooden rock are one row each, and so adding a family to scatter.json surfaces here as a failing test rather than as a silent dull hit. Every harvestable family in harvest.json must appear.
